question: What is the stage on which the cosmic dancer performs the world-drama?
premises: The stage is called raṅga because the Self delights to display the play of the world-drama there.
This stage is the inner self, appearing as contraction in the form of breath, the eightfold subtle city, and the regulated individual soul.
Through the vibration of its own faculties, which is the flashing forth of innate freedom, the individual makes the world-drama appear on this inner stage.
inference: Therefore the inner self functions as the stage on which the dancing Lord manifests the drama of the universe.
plain_english: The commentary explains that the stage of the cosmic dance is the inner self. It is called a stage because the Self takes delight in displaying the drama of the world there. This inner self appears in a contracted form as the individual soul, shaped by breath and the subtle eightfold apparatus. On that inner stage, through the vibration of its own faculties, the Self makes the whole world-drama appear.
